title: IDF Drone Kills Hamas Police Colonel Naseem al-Kalazani; At Least 5 Palestinians Killed in Gaza Strikes
detail: At least five Palestinians were killed in Israeli strikes across Gaza on May 6, 2026, in the largest single-day toll since the October 2025 ceasefire. The most significant strike was a targeted Israeli drone attack on the vehicle of Naseem al-Kalazani — a colonel commanding Hamas's anti-narcotics police force in Khan Younis — near the al-Mawasi coastal area. At least 17 others were wounded in the strike. Separate Israeli attacks on the same day included: a strike on the Sheikh Radwan neighborhood in northwestern Gaza City that killed one Palestinian and wounded two others; Israeli tank shelling in central Gaza that killed another Palestinian; and a strike on a police station in northern Gaza that killed a 15-year-old. Gaza's Civil Defence confirmed all deaths and transported victims to Nasser, Al-Shifa, and Al-Ahli hospitals. The IDF characterized all targets as Hamas-affiliated 'armed operatives.' The Gaza Government Media Office updated the cumulative ceasefire death toll to 834 Palestinians killed since the October 10, 2025 ceasefire took effect. RTÉ and Democracy Now! both confirmed the figures from local Palestinian health officials. The ICRC expressed concern that daily Israeli strikes were incompatible with the ceasefire framework and called for urgent adherence to international humanitarian law. The Hamas Government Information Office accused Israel of attempting to collapse the ceasefire from within through targeted killings while avoiding overt full-scale military operations.

media.caption: IDF drone kills Hamas police colonel Naseem al-Kalazani near al-Mawasi; at least 5 Palestinians killed across Gaza — May 6, 2026

title: IDF Airstrike Wounds Azzam Al-Hayya, Son of Senior Hamas Negotiator Khalil Al-Hayya
detail: An Israeli airstrike on May 6, 2026 injured Azzam Al-Hayya, the son of Khalil Al-Hayya — one of Hamas's most senior political officials and the movement's chief negotiator in disarmament talks with the Board of Peace. The strike killed at least one other person in Gaza City and wounded several others. RTÉ confirmed the wounding of Azzam Al-Hayya from Palestinian medical sources. Khalil Al-Hayya, who is based in Doha, Qatar, had previously lost three sons in IDF operations during the Gaza war; the wounding of Azzam Al-Hayya was his fourth family member to be directly targeted or harmed by Israeli fire. The timing — occurring on the same day as the Board of Peace ultimatum over Hamas disarmament — was widely noted by analysts as a signal of Israeli willingness to continue targeting Hamas political figures and their families even during ceasefire negotiations. Hamas's Information Office accused Israel of trying to assassinate the negotiating team's families as a form of intimidation. The Israeli Prime Minister's Office did not publicly comment on the specific strike targeting Azzam Al-Hayya.

media.caption: IDF strike wounds son of Hamas negotiator Khalil Al-Hayya — Khalil has now lost four family members to Israeli fire

title: UN Human Rights Office Demands Israel Immediately and Unconditionally Release Gaza Flotilla Activists
detail: The United Nations Human Rights Office (OHCHR) formally demanded on May 6, 2026 that Israel 'immediately and unconditionally' release flotilla activists Saif Abu Keshek and Thiago Ávila. OHCHR spokesperson Thameen Al-Kheetan issued the statement after an Israeli court extended both men's detention until May 10 without charge. The UN statement noted that both men had alleged abuse — including being held in stress positions, blindfolded, and subjected to sleep deprivation — and called on Israel to conduct an immediate, independent investigation into the abuse claims. Al Jazeera reported the full OHCHR statement. The UN Human Rights Office cited both Israeli law and UNCLOS, under which the flotilla interception in international waters may have been unlawful, as grounds for immediate release. The statement also noted that the Global Sumud Flotilla was carrying humanitarian aid intended for Gaza under a recognized international relief framework. The European Parliament passed a non-binding resolution the same day calling on EU member states to impose targeted sanctions on Israeli officials responsible for ordering the flotilla interception, though the resolution is not legally binding on national governments. UK Foreign Secretary David Lammy separately called the ongoing detention 'deeply troubling' and urged Israel to allow full consular access to both men.

media.caption: UN Human Rights Office demands Israel immediately release flotilla activists Abu Keshek and Ávila — May 6, 2026

title: Board of Peace Publishes Formal Ultimatum: Hamas Must Disarm or Lose All Ceasefire Guarantees
detail: The Trump-backed Board of Peace (BoP) formally published its position on May 6, 2026: Hamas must accept the five-stage disarmament roadmap 'or the Board of Peace will no longer hold Israel to its ceasefire commitments.' The ultimatum, confirmed by the Times of Israel and Hot Air, marked the first time the BoP had publicly linked its own mediation role to Hamas's compliance with disarmament as a precondition — a significant escalation of the diplomatic pressure. The statement was issued as High Representative Nickolay Mladenov briefed US Special Envoy Steve Witkoff by phone from Tel Aviv after his May 5 meeting with Netanyahu. The BoP's position aligned closely with the Netanyahu government's longstanding demand that Hamas disarmament must precede any further Israeli compliance with Phase 2 of the October 2025 ceasefire agreement. The Palestinian Authority's Foreign Ministry condemned the BoP ultimatum as 'one-sided and a betrayal of the ceasefire guarantors' role.' Egypt and Qatar — the two primary non-US mediators of the October 2025 ceasefire — issued a joint statement on May 6 warning that any formal collapse of the ceasefire framework would have 'catastrophic consequences for regional stability' and calling on all parties to recommit to the original ceasefire terms without preconditions.

media.caption: Board of Peace publishes formal ultimatum to Hamas: disarm or lose all ceasefire guarantees — May 6, 2026
